chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Sharif ibn Sabiq, from Al-Fadl ibn Abi Qurra, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The best time for you to supplicate to Allah, Exalted and Majestic, is the pre-dawn hours.'
And he recited this verse regarding the words of Yaqoub (peace be upon him): 'Soon I will ask for your forgiveness from my Lord.'
And he said: 'He delayed them until the pre-dawn.'

key_terms.السَّحَرِ: The pre-dawn period, specifically the time just before dawn
key_terms.الْأَسْحَارُ: The pre-dawn hours, the last part of the night before Fajr prayer
key_terms.سَوْفَ أَسْتَغْفِرُ لَكُمْ رَبِّي: Soon I will ask for your forgiveness from my Lord (Quran 12:98)

ai.seo_question: What is the best time of day for supplication according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) highlights the pre-dawn hours (Al-Sahar) as the most auspicious time for supplication, linking it to the verse where Prophet Yaqoub (peace be upon him) promised to seek forgiveness for his children. This narration underscores the spiritual significance of the last third of the night, a period revered in Shia tradition for its closeness to divine acceptance and the transition from night to day. The reference to Yaqoub’s promise illustrates the virtue of persisting in intercession until the final moments before dawn, reinforcing the practice of Tahajjud and Du'a in the quiet hours.
